chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
When the redness disappears from this side — meaning from the east — then the sun has indeed set from the east of the earth and from its west.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose setting determines the prayer time
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: the redness or red glow seen in the sky after sunset
key_terms.الْمَشْرِقِ: the east; the direction from which the redness is observed
key_terms.شَرْقِ الْأَرْضِ: the east of the earth; indicating complete sunset
key_terms.غَابَتِ: disappeared; used here for the vanishing of a visible sign
key_terms.غَرْبِهَا: its west; paired with east to emphasize the sun’s full setting

ai.seo_question: How is the time of maghrib determined according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a sign for determining the time of maghrib: the disappearance of the eastern redness after sunset. It serves as a jurisprudential indicator for the onset of the evening prayer time in Shia fiqh.
